findings.title: Fallback chain depends on per-site default_locale but the translation LRU cache ignores it
findings.body:
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds the fallback chain from `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which differs per site in multisite and can be changed by an admin at runtime. The process-wide LRU cache in `I18n.translate` (translate_accelerator.rb, `k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`) is keyed only by key, requested locale and backend.

Scenario: a user on site A (default `de`) requests a key that is missing in `ja`. The `de` fallback string is cached. A `ja` user on site B (default `fr`) in the same process then gets site A's German text. The same staleness happens after an admin changes `default_locale`: earlier fallback results stay cached until the process restarts.

Fix: include the resolved fallback chain (or the site default locale) in the cache key, or skip caching results that came from a fallback.

findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in ApplicationController, so other contexts miss fallbacks and can poison the cache
findings.body:
The patched loader only loads translation files on demand. `I18n.translate` loads `config.locale` only, and the fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. These paths never call it:
- Sidekiq jobs and mailers
- rake tasks
- controllers or middleware outside ApplicationController
- `I18n.t(..., locale: x)` calls

In those paths a key missing from the current locale falls back to locales whose translations were never loaded, so the lookup returns "translation missing: ...". For argument-less `I18n.t` calls that string is frozen into the shared LRU cache under `key+locale`. Later web requests get the cached "translation missing" text even after `ensure_loaded!` has loaded `en`.

Fix: load the fallback chain inside the patched `I18n.translate` / `load_locale`, not in a controller filter.
